audit_findings.title: The historical OE series may cross the Fortrea spin-off on an inconsistent perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially distorts the historical OE trend used to select growth rates; it does not alter the $629.6 million post-spin anchor directly.
audit_findings.evidence: On June 30, 2023, the Company completed the separation of Fortrea, formerly the Company’s CDCS business, into a separate, publicly traded company.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated error. The filing says Fortrea was classified as discontinued operations and presented historical results on that basis, but the record does not establish that every 2016-2022 OE observation was rebuilt from the recast cash-flow components. A constant-perimeter history could support either higher or lower growth. Because the effect on the selected growth scenarios cannot be computed from the supplied record, materiality remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2016-2022 OE from continuing-operation cash flows on a Fortrea-excluded basis, document each recast component, and rerun growth selection and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 numerator and June 2026 balance-sheet bridge omit an intervening acquisition perimeter change
audit_findings.magnitude: $528.6 million total 2026 acquisition consideration, including $428.3 million cash paid and $75.7 million contingent consideration; $6.20 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: The June 2026 cash, debt, contingent liabilities, and share count reflect acquisitions absent from FY2025 OE, creating inconsistent numerator and bridge dates.
audit_findings.evidence: The Empire City transaction closed during the first quarter of 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporal mismatch is demonstrated. Its direction is mixed because omitted acquired earnings understate value, while omitted post-close financing costs can overstate OE; acquisition cash payments already reduce the bridge cash. The entire $528.6 million consideration equals about 5.7% of the $9,198 million base value and $6.20 per 85.2 million shares, versus a $206.82 per-share gap between the $120.07 bull value and the $326.89 market price. Filed pro forma first-half 2026 net earnings were only $8.2 million above reported earnings. On the filed scale, this mismatch is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Prepare either a fully pro forma FY2025 OE numerator including all 2026 acquisitions, financing costs, and contingent consideration, or roll cash, debt, liabilities, and shares back to December 31, 2025; confirm the conclusion remains unchanged.

audit_findings.title: The Ravgen judgment and continuing royalty may be an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $374.6 million of awarded damages plus unquantified interest and a filed $100-per-test continuing royalty
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid judgment belongs in the equity bridge, while continuing royalties reduce forward OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In May 2023, the court awarded Ravgen additional enhanced damages in the amount of $100.0 million, and in January 2025, the court awarded Ravgen post-verdict supplemental damages of $2.6 million, an ongoing royalty of $100 per test through the life of the patent as issue, pre- and post-judgement interest, and other relief.
audit_findings.explanation: The $272.0 million verdict, $100.0 million enhanced damages, and $2.6 million supplemental damages are demonstrated, but the record does not show the net unpaid amount, related accrual, insurance recovery, or royalty-bearing test volume. The quantified awards alone equal $4.40 per valuation share and would not close the $206.82 gap between bull value and market price. The recurring royalty could be more important because it affects every projected year and terminal value, but its volume and duration are not quantified; therefore overall materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the awards, accrued interest, appeal bond, insurance, payments, and June 2026 legal accrual; obtain royalty-bearing test volumes and patent expiration, then deduct the net unpaid claim and rerun OE with the royalty expense.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may use a temporarily low capital-spending run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $123.6 million computed increase from 3.1% to 4.0% of FY2025 revenue; first-half 2026 capex was $252.6 million or 3.5% of revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring maintenance portion of the higher spending reduces forward OE dollar-for-dollar before growth is applied.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects this level of spending to increase in 2026 to 4.0%, primarily in connection with projects to support growth in the Company’s core businesses, facility expansion and updates, projects related to its LaunchPad initiative, and further acquisition integration initiatives.
audit_findings.explanation: No current calculation error is demonstrated because the 4.0% disclosure is a forward spending plan and expressly includes growth, facility, LaunchPad, and acquisition-integration projects. Applied to FY2025 revenue, 4.0% is approximately $558.1 million, $123.6 million above filed FY2025 capex of $434.5 million and equal to 19.6% of the $629.6 million anchor. First-half 2026 spending confirms an increase but does not identify maintenance capex, so this should be monitored rather than treated as a presently proven adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Use full-year or trailing-twelve-month 2026 capex disclosures to separate maintenance from growth and integration spending, then rerun OE if recurring maintenance exceeds the FY2025 amount.

audit_findings.title: SYNLAB may be counted inconsistently between OE and the stakes bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.3 million FY2025 equity-method loss, $11.3 million first-half 2026 equity-method loss, and $139.3 million June 2026 carrying value of all joint ventures and equity-method investments
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained equity-method results affect OE and its projected growth, while separately adding the same investment value in the bridge would double count its economics.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in Equity method loss, net for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared with the corresponding period in 2024, was primarily due to the loss recognized from the SYNLAB investment that closed in the first quarter of 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential inconsistency is unresolved. The filing identifies SYNLAB as the principal cause of equity-method losses, but it does not show the OE worksheet or prove that SYNLAB is included in the $210 million stakes bridge. The filed $210 million carrying value for other non-equity-method investments suggests the bridge may exclude SYNLAB, but that correspondence is not conclusive. Retaining losses without adding the stake can understate value; retaining stake economics and adding its value can overstate value. The record cannot establish the net effect or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Produce an investment-by-investment bridge identifying SYNLAB, reconcile the $210 million stakes amount to filed carrying values, and rerun OE after removing equity-method earnings, losses, distributions, and related taxes for every separately valued stake.

audit_findings.title: The Ontario noncontrolling-interest put is a separate senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.4 million at June 30, 2026, or $0.19 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: The contractual redemption claim should reduce value attributable to common equity unless already netted in another bridge item.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has a noncontrolling interest put option related to its Ontario subsidiary that has been classified as mezzanine equity in the Company’s Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed $16.4 million mezzanine-equity put is demonstrated and the supplied bridge does not expressly deduct it. Even if wholly omitted, it equals about 0.18% of the $9,198 million base equity value and $0.19 per 85.2 million shares, versus the $206.82 gap between bull value and market price. It cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the $16.4 million put is not already included in stakes_net or another bridge line; if not, deduct it from common-equity value in the next rerun.
